headline: High: Cursor’s filesystem/MCP/browserless agent can leak or corrupt Kotaemon’s shared workspace and API-key-bearing documents by default; prompt-injection and cascading errors are also plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads and writes workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and can use MCP; kotaemon ingests documents, PDFs, HTML, chat transcripts, and API keys via web UI. A malicious document or copied content from Cursor can be treated as instructions by kotaemon, and shared local files create a direct bridge. The interaction is plausible in default workflows, though not proven by sandbox evidence.
conditions: IF Cursor content is copied into kotaemon chat or indexed documents are opened in kotaemon, prompt-like text can steer downstream behavior.
IF both agents access the same local workspace or ./ktem_app_data, attacker-controlled file content can bridge them.
mitigations: Disable shared-folder access between the editor workspace and kotaemon data directory.
Strip instructions from imported documents before indexing.
Use a separate, read-only staging folder for files passed from Cursor to kotaemon.
Turn off MCP servers not needed for the task.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels so kotaemon ignores instructions from untrusted documents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and model-provider APIs; kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys while also calling external LLM APIs. If they share files or clipboard, sensitive code or keys can flow from Cursor into kotaemon and then to third-party inference backends. That is a default-dangerous leakage path with broad blast radius.
conditions: IF Cursor and kotaemon are pointed at the same workspace or data folder, files containing secrets can be read by both.
IF kotaemon indexes uploaded documents containing API keys or transcripts, those contents can be sent to external model providers.
mitigations: Keep kotaemon and Cursor on separate directories.
Remove secrets from documents before upload or indexing.
Rotate any API keys that may have been exposed in shared files.
Disable clipboard-based transfer between the tools during sensitive work.
requires-engineering: enforce per-tool data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted local write, shell, git, and broad network egress; kotaemon writes to ./ktem_app_data and can call external APIs. Their write surfaces overlap only if the same filesystem tree or repo is shared, but Cursor’s per-window local state via filesystem makes that plausible. The conflict is real but not guaranteed in every deployment, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or shared data directory, concurrent writes can clobber files.
IF Cursor auto-runs commands in Yolo mode while kotaemon updates its app data, state races can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories to each agent.
Avoid running Cursor in Yolo mode on shared repos.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the same tree.
Use git branches or locks for shared mutable files.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code, facts, and edits; kotaemon is a web UI RAG/chat system that can present retrieved content and act on it through downstream user workflows. If Cursor-produced output is imported into kotaemon without verification, kotaemon may render or rely on it as authoritative. The pair lacks explicit verification or provenance controls in the profiles, so cascading error is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Cursor-generated text or code is pasted into kotaemon as source material, kotaemon may surface it as trusted context.
IF kotaemon outputs are used to drive follow-on actions without human review, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on kotaemon outputs.
Mark Cursor-generated artifacts as untrusted input in kotaemon.
Use citations or source links when importing content.
Separate draft and approved knowledge bases.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware ranking and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, clipboard contents, and model-provider APIs; kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and may send them to OpenAI/Azure/Cohere/Groq. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data is moved between them. Because the exact jurisdictional constraints are unknown, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are indexed in kotaemon and also opened in Cursor, retention and logging obligations may diverge.
IF either deployment is subject to residency or deletion requirements, the profiles do not show matching controls.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflows.
Review vendor retention and logging settings before use.
Use separate tenants or deployments for sensitive data.
Delete temporary transcripts and caches after each session.
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention policy mapping.
